text:
devon: Heads up — seeing gRPC streaming stalls on inference pods across nodes in eu-west-1. Starts when model output is large (20-40KB chunks). Same-node traffic looks fine.

maya: Is this across AZs or within the same AZ?

devon: Same AZ mostly, but definitely east-west (pod->pod on different nodes). Client logs show repeated RST_STREAM / stream closed errors.

kevin: Can you share tcpdump and MTU info from the host + pod?

devon: Pasting a few snippets.

```
# ip link show on nodeA
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:01 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
14: cali12345: mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default
    link/ether 12:34:56:78:9a:bc brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
```

```
# tcpdump (filtered) showing DF and ICMP frag_needed
IP 10.10.1.12.50052 > 10.10.3.9.54782: Flags [P.], seq 1:1501, win 501, length 1500
ICMP 10.10.3.9 > 10.10.1.12: frag needed and DF set (type 3/4)
```

```
# ping test to podIP with don't fragment
ping -M do -s 8972 10.10.3.9
PING 10.10.3.9 (10.10.3.9) 8972(9000) bytes of data.
From 10.10.1.1 icmp_seq=1 Frag needed and DF set
```

maya: So host NICs are jumbo (9000) but the overlay veth/cali is 1500 -> fragmentation when packets cross the CNI. The ICMP frag-needed is being sent but looks like something else is dropping it (or nodes have PMTU discovery disabled).

jia: We should check net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc and host firewall/security-groups for ICMP type 3 code 4. IIRC we had a kernel tweak on one image that set ip_no_pmtu_disc=1.

kevin: Confirmed on nodeB: sysctl shows ip_no_pmtu_disc = 1. Also our cloud SG was blocking ICMP in the old hardened baseline. That explains blackholing.

jia: Quick mitigation steps:
- enable PMTU discovery on affected nodes: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=0`
- allow ICMP frag-needed (type 3 code 4) in node firewall / SGs
- short-term traffic steering: schedule affinity so streaming happens intra-node or force same-node through topologyHint (fastest workaround)

devon: Trying sysctl now on a canary node + allowing ICMP on host firewall.

```
# enable PMTU discovery
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=0
# iptables rule (host firewall)
sudo iptables -I INPUT -p icmp --icmp-type fragmentation-needed -j ACCEPT
```

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1874 — High gRPC streaming latencies (eu-west-1). Pager duty alerted.

kevin: Long-term fix options:
- standardize MTU across stack (set CNI MTU to 9000 if you have jumbo frame support across switches) OR lower host MTU to 1500 cluster-wide to avoid cross-MTU fragmentation.
- update cluster bootstrap to verify ip_no_pmtu_disc=0 and ICMP allowed for PMTU discovery.
- add a network test in our e2e infra that pings pods with large MTU to catch regressions.

jia: For Calico/VXLAN specifically, set the CNI MTU so overlay fits under host MTU (e.g., calicoctl patch felixconfiguration default --patch '{"spec":{"mtu":9000}}') OR set CNI MTU to 1450/1500 depending on encapsulation.

devon: After enabling PMTU and opening ICMP on the canary, gRPC streams no longer stall for ~30m test. Rolling the sysctl + firewall change to remaining nodes.

maya: Nice. Can we do a short config change window to standardize to 1500 across nodes? It's lower-risk than relying on jumbo frames across all racks and avoids future frag issues.

kevin: Agree. I'll schedule a change to set host MTU to 1500 cluster-wide and align CNI MTU during next maintenance window. We'll also add the PMTU checks to kube-prober.

devon: Thanks team. Leaving the incident open until change window completes. Will post follow-up notes in the incident doc. :thumbsup:
